gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ discussing one agenda item for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour' and still relevant — present perfect continuous.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.sentence: This perfume ___ of roses and vanilla.
gaps.hint: perceived smell is a state verb
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'smell' are state verbs, so the present simple is used: smells.

gaps.sentence: I ___ exactly what you mean, so there is no need to explain again.
gaps.explanation: 'Understand' is a state verb and is not used in continuous forms, so the present simple is correct.
